title: Seedling emergence after four seed treatments
bodyMd: A dormant wildflower seed faces two separate obstacles: a hard seed coat that water cannot cross, and a chemical dormancy that a long cold period removes. Horticulturist Ola Berg planted 200 seeds under each of four treatments and counted the seedlings that emerged within 21 days.

data.caption: Seedling emergence within 21 days for four seed treatments, 200 seeds planted per treatment (Berg).

accessibilityText: A four-row table titled "Seedling emergence after four seed treatments". Columns are seed treatment, seeds planted, seedlings emerged within 21 days, and emergence rate as a percent. Every treatment used 200 seeds. No treatment: 34 seedlings, 17.0 percent. Scarified, meaning the seed coat was nicked: 96 seedlings, 48.0 percent. Cold-stratified for 90 days: 122 seedlings, 61.0 percent. Scarified and cold-stratified together: 131 seedlings, 65.5 percent.

provenance.notes: Original table written for this item bank. The horticulturist, the experiment and all counts are invented; the numbers were chosen so that each comparison the questions ask about is unambiguous.
